title: Drinking gin and playing mellophone with Bix and Carl
summary: Bix, Carl and Davison buy bathtub gin, play in a parked car and at an after-hours Black club called the Hole in the Wall.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, why don't you tell us some of those stories - you got to be pretty good pals with Bix ---

Yes - I got to play with him a lot because we used to go to the same place together - to buy our gin - in those days and, uh, with Carl, who was quite a drinker himself and, of course, everybody knows that Bix drank a lot---

And, uh, I wasn't so far behind in those days either. But, we used to go to this big fat lady--- she lived in not Walnut Hills --but Price Hill and that was quite a ways; it was a big, big hill in Cincinnati and we used to go up there and buy the gin for a dollar a pint and sometimes, we'd each buy ten or twelve depending on how much money we had of those pints. But, during that time, I played a lot of things I never had the courage to play with-- the cornet along

side of Vicks at that point because I certainly wasn't anything near that. But, I could play the mellophone and I could play the trombone parts on the mellophone - and, so, Carl would get his banjo out and Bix get his horn out and we're sitting in the car drinking this terrible bathtub gin and I'd play the mellophone and I wish we had-- I kind of wish there was tapes in those days because we played some very pretty little things together.

Yeah. And, I remember there was another place that we used to go; we used to love to go there -- it was an all colored place -- it was called "The Hole in the Wall" and we used to go there once in awhile and, of course, the boss was delighted to see us and the only thing they sold in there was gin and pork chop sandwiches and we'd--- we liked a place to play -- just to, you know, an after-hours thing and---
This was very early in the morning ---

Oh, yeah - two, three o'clock in the morning. And, they were delighted to see us and we'd go in there and sit in the corner - banjo, mellophone and cornet and play a few songs; of course, we got everything for nothing - you know. And, I did that many times and, then, of course, during that time, Bix had--- about in that time, the Wolverines left the Stockton Club. Now, I don't know why.
